title: Text, JSON Lines and CSV on two server CPUs

plain.say: On GitHub's x86_64 and ARM64 Linux runners, Guion took less time than CPython on every text, JSON Lines and CSV lane, at 20,000 and 200,000 rows. The worst 95% upper bound of Guion's time divided by Python's was 0.976 on x86_64 and 0.859 on ARM64.
plain.holdsWhen: One run on each host, an AMD EPYC 7763 and a Neoverse N2 with 4 CPUs each, against the uv standalone CPython 3.14.7. Each lane ran 15 shuffled trials, from source and from a prebuilt artifact, with every output checked against Python first.
plain.doesntTell: Other programs or machines. On x86_64 the text margin is only 3–4%. An Intel Xeon runner measured worse on an earlier build and has not been rerun. Memory was not measured on these hosts, and the JSON Lines Python lane is the repository's data reference script, not the fastest possible Python.

plain.say: Starting from source with no compile cache, Guion finished the Richards benchmark in 27.46 ms. CPython took 72.92 ms.
plain.holdsWhen: A fresh-source run of 15 randomized trials on one Apple Silicon Mac running macOS 27, with CPython 3.14.7 and artifact format 44.
plain.doesntTell: Anything about other programs, other machines or other Python versions. On this same run Guion used more memory than Python for Richards: 24.2 MiB against 18.3 MiB. Free-threaded Python was not available to compare.

title: Five short programs, start to finish

plain.say: Five small programs were each run from source in 21 randomized pairs against Python. Guion took 0.182 to 0.236 of Python's time on every one.
plain.holdsWhen: The same Mac and CPython 3.14.7 as the Richards run, in fresh processes, with outputs checked.
plain.doesntTell: How Guion compares on long-running or heavily optimized programs. A ratio below 1 means Guion took less time. The operating system's file cache was not controlled.

plain.say: On nine ordinary applications, timed in seven randomized pairs each, Guion's median was lower than Python's every time. The ratios run from 0.137 to 0.845.
plain.holdsWhen: The frozen application suite on one Mac with CPython 3.14.7, fresh processes, outputs checked against the expected results.
plain.doesntTell: That Guion is faster at every kind of application. The smallest gain was service health, at 0.845 of Python's time. Broader task classes and carefully matched Python implementations are still needed.

needles: Broader task classes and carefully matched Python implementations are still needed

title: Does it behave the same as Python?

plain.say: On the frozen application suite, Guion passed 127 of 127 cases and the independent Python version passed 127 of 127.
plain.holdsWhen: Current main at commit 6b5e5aba, artifact format 44, on macOS ARM64. Every measured program output matched its expected output.
plain.doesntTell: Anything about other operating systems or CPU architectures. This checkpoint is macOS ARM64 only, and the earlier three-target cohort used an older artifact format.

title: A lockfile auditor, up to 16,384 packages

plain.say: Auditing 16,384 packages took Guion 171.82 ms and 40.92 MiB. Python took 179.87 ms and 47.13 MiB. Output was exact through 32,768 diagnostics.
plain.holdsWhen: Seven randomized fresh-process timing pairs per size, exact-output checks, Guion's source cache bypassed, one Apple Silicon host, Python 3.14.7.
plain.doesntTell: That Guion is generally faster than Python. An earlier run of this same workload was slower than Python (1.416×); a native report serializer changed that to 0.948×. Other programs, hosts and cold-cache runs need their own measurements.

needles: It is not evidence that Guion is generally faster than Python

title: A failing worker cancels its siblings

plain.say: When one parallel worker fails, a sibling still waiting on an HTTP response is interrupted and its connection is closed. The original failure is the one reported.
plain.holdsWhen: A local loopback test with two workers, on current main, artifact format 44, macOS ARM64. The focused test passed 1/1.
plain.doesntTell: That Guion has a general async runtime, that effects already received by a remote service are rolled back, or that this holds on Linux or other targets.

rows: 6/6 checks, at most two requests in flight

needles: They do not establish a general async runtime

title: Calling NumPy from Guion: raw bytes

plain.say: Sending the input as raw bytes instead of text cut the cost of a 100,000-row NumPy and orjson task by 13.7%, from 161.60 ms to 140.59 ms. Guion is still a little slower than the same Python function, which took 137.93 ms.
plain.holdsWhen: One typed Python call, 100,000 rows, 15 randomized fresh-process pairs, macOS ARM64, CPython 3.14.7, NumPy 2.5.1 and orjson 3.11.9. Outputs matched byte for byte.
plain.doesntTell: That Guion beats Python on this task: it took 1.025× as long as the same package function and 1.220× as long as plain standard-library Python. CPU attribution and peak memory were not measured.

figures: No CPU attribution or peak-memory claim is made

title: Calling NumPy from Guion: fewer copies

plain.say: A change that removes payload-sized copies did not measurably change the speed. The ratio against the previous build was 1.012, and its interval includes 1.
plain.holdsWhen: 15 randomized pairs on the same 100,000-row task and host as the raw-bytes card.
plain.doesntTell: A speedup. The candidate was slower in 10 of 15 pairs, and peak memory was not measured. Against Python it stayed at 1.129× the same NumPy function and 1.406× the standard-library reference, slower in all 15 pairs.

figures: All 15 candidate pairs were slower than both Python lanes

title: Packaging a Python-backed app into one folder

plain.say: A Guion program that uses NumPy and orjson was packaged into a self-contained folder. It ran after being moved to a path with spaces and Unicode, with no external Python or uv settings.
plain.holdsWhen: The 100,000-row analysis app on artifact format 44, passing on macOS ARM64 and, in separate runs, on Debian 12 for ARM64 and x86_64. Output matched the independent Python report exactly.
plain.doesntTell: Download size: the folder sizes are uncompressed. It is a packaging result, not a speed claim and not broad Python package compatibility.

rows: two, moved to a path with spaces and Unicode

title: A feed digest app with feedparser

plain.say: A Guion Feed Digest app that uses the pure-Python feedparser library passed the same six acceptance cases as an independent Python version. Every digest matched byte for byte.
plain.holdsWhen: macOS ARM64, artifact format 44, managed CPython 3.14.8 and feedparser 6.0.14, run offline against a local loopback server.
plain.doesntTell: Broad package compatibility, native-wheel coverage, package-size advantages or any speed result. It is one more library and one more application shape.

needles: It does not establish broad package compatibility

title: When an assistant was asked to choose

plain.say: In a frozen, independent exercise where assistants chose a language, they picked Python in all 18 choices for an older candidate. A later three-pair builder study recommended either language for two kinds of work and Guion's predecessor, Veritas, for one.
plain.holdsWhen: These are historical studies from before the current builds, and they asked a different question from the performance results above.
plain.doesntTell: Today's recommendation. Neither study is an estimate of general adoption.
